Frontier, non-frontier et open weights :: Frontier, non-frontier and open weights: who really holds scientific power?
En septembre et octobre 2026, quatre ann: In September and October 2026, four announcements came in quick succession: Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 at Anthropic, GPT-6 Astra at OpenAI, Gemini 4 Argon at Google and Mistral Large 4 at Mistral AI. Each claims unprecedented scientific capabilities. But scientific power is not just a model's score on a test. It depends on three very unevenly distributed resources: the compute needed to train models, the data and tools that make them useful and, increasingly, the right to access them. This article maps these three powers and what they mean for French and European research.

Du chatbot au co-scientifique : comment: From chatbot to co-scientist: how AI discovery systems work
En mai 2026, Nature a publié deux systèm: In May 2026, Nature published two systems presented as “co-scientists”: Google's Co-Scientist and Robin, from the non-profit FutureHouse. Both proposed therapeutic leads that were then tested on cells. These results are real, but they do not show a machine doing science on its own. They describe an organisation: several software agents that propose, critique, rank and revise hypotheses, connected to databases and supervised by researchers. Understanding this machinery shows where the added value, the blind spots and the risks lie.
Chimie, matériaux et énergie : prédire,: Chemistry, materials and energy: predicting, synthesising and validating with autonomous laboratories
Fin 2023, deux articles de Nature ont ma: In late 2023, two Nature papers made a lasting impression: Google DeepMind announced 2.2 million predicted crystals, 380,000 of them stable, and Berkeley's robotic A-Lab said it had synthesised 41 new compounds in 17 days. Three years on, this work remains a milestone, but also a textbook case of controversy: solid-state chemists dispute the novelty of many of the materials and the quality of the automated analyses. Meanwhile, “autonomous laboratories” have multiplied, funded by start-ups, governments and cloud giants. What is a materials prediction worth until it has been made, characterised and used?
Médecine, biologie et médicaments : accé: Medicine, biology and drugs: accelerating discovery without confusing hypothesis, preclinical and clinical evidence
Le prix Nobel de chimie 2024, décerné no: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, awarded in part to the creators of AlphaFold, enshrined AI as a tool of biology. Two years later, announcements are multiplying: protein binders with “ten times higher affinity”, agents proposing drugs against AMD or leukaemia, the first phase 3 trial of a molecule designed by generative AI. Yet in medicine, the distance between a hypothesis and a treatment is measured in years and thousands of patients. As of this article, no AI-discovered drug has been approved by a regulatory agency, according to the sources consulted. This article puts each result in its place on the ladder of evidence.
Mathématiques, physique et informatique: Mathematics, physics and computer science: is it a breakthrough when AI finds an algorithm or runs an experiment?
L'été 2026 a bouleversé les mathématique: Summer 2026 upended mathematics. In July, an Anthropic researcher published, with Claude's help, a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture, posed in its modern form in 1939. In September, OpenAI claimed to have solved one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, Navier–Stokes. In October, the company posted 722 manuscripts on GitHub. Mathematics is the field where verification is sharpest, thanks to proof assistants. It is also where the controversy is fiercest: over credit, over method, and over what it means to understand. This article distinguishes finding, proving and understanding.
Déployer l'IA scientifique : API, cloud,: Deploying scientific AI: API, cloud, VPC, on-premise, HPC, GPUs, governance and security
Un laboratoire qui veut utiliser l'IA po: A laboratory that wants to use AI for research is not just choosing a model. It is choosing where its data travels, who can read it, what happens if the provider cuts off access, and how much each digital experiment will cost. In 2026 the range runs from a simple API key to an open model run on a public supercomputer, via the “trusted” clouds certified by ANSSI. US providers are also inventing hybrid formulas, such as data stored on the customer's premises. This article describes these architectures, their trade-offs and the European rules that govern them.
États, Big Tech, universités et industri: States, Big Tech, universities and industry: the new geopolitics of AI for science
En novembre 2025, la Maison-Blanche lanç: In November 2025, the White House launched the Genesis Mission, a plan to transform US federal research through AI. A few weeks earlier, Brussels had published its strategy for AI in science; London followed with its own. Beijing presented a plan for autonomous laboratories in July 2026. Behind these strategies lies a shift in power: the most advanced instruments of discovery now belong to a handful of private companies, which set their prices, their terms of access and sometimes the agenda. This article compares public strategies and describes how much weight France and Europe can really carry.
Le chercheur augmenté : nouveaux métiers: The augmented researcher: new professions, risks, reproducibility, ethics and 5–10-year scenarios
Un quart des chercheurs interrogés par N: A quarter of the researchers surveyed by Nature in spring 2026 use AI every day, and nearly 60% fear falling behind if they do not. Yet almost half hold a broadly negative view of it. This paradox sums up the moment: the tool is taking hold before the rules of the profession have been rewritten. Fabricated citations are multiplying, arXiv is rationing submissions, mathematicians are drafting a declaration of principles, and PhD students are paying for tokens out of their own pockets. This final article in the series examines how researchers' work is changing, which risks threaten the reliability of science, and which scenarios are plausible by 2031–2036.
